issue: The EC IUP projects (tx_ec / SFY 2025 EC IUP) have no PIF number column in the source data according to the dictionary ('No information for projects in the SFY25 EC IUP'), yet the script attempts to populate project_id via str_squish(pif_number) for all rows. EC IUP rows will silently produce NA/No Information rather than raising a clear flag.
suggestion: Add an explicit comment or conditional check confirming that EC IUP rows are expected to have no PIF number, and document that project_id = 'No Information' is the correct fallback for those rows.

issue: tx_ec_invite is joined to tx_ec by 'rank' only. If two EC projects share the same rank value (e.g., ties or data entry issues), the join could incorrectly assign 'Yes' to wrong projects or produce duplicate rows.
suggestion: Verify that 'rank' is unique in the EC invite list, or add a deduplication step before the join. Consider also joining on an additional key if available.

issue: tx_lsl_invite is joined to tx_lsl by both 'pif_no' and 'rank'. The dictionary states that the LSLR invite list is Appendix J of the SFY25 LSLR IUP and that projects not on that list get 'No'. If rank or pif_no differ between the priority list and invite list due to amendments, valid invited projects could be missed.
suggestion: After the join, verify that the number of 'Yes' rows in tx_lsl matches the expected count from the LSLR invite appendix.

issue: The grepl pattern for Lead is 'lsl|lead' but the dictionary specifies the trigger keywords as 'lead' or 'LSLR'. The pattern 'lsl' (lowercase, partial) could match unintended substrings (e.g., 'vessel', 'dissolved'). Additionally the dictionary explicitly uses 'LSLR' not 'lsl'.
suggestion: Change the pattern to 'LSLR|lead' with ignore.case = TRUE, or use word-boundary anchors to avoid false positives: grepl('\\bLSLR\\b|\\blead\\b', project_description, ignore.case = TRUE).

issue: The script references an object 'ec_str' that is not defined within the function. If it is defined in the global environment, this creates a hidden dependency that could break or silently use a stale/incorrect pattern.
suggestion: Define ec_str explicitly inside the function with all dictionary-specified keywords: 'cyanotoxin|dioxane|emerging contaminant|lithium|manganese|\\bMn\\b|Perfluoro-n-pentanoic acid|PFPeA|PFAS|PFOA|PFOS|trihalomethane|\\bTHM\\b|Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule'.

issue: For general project types, the dictionary says: if 'Disadv %' has a value then disadvantaged = 'Yes'. The script checks is.na(disadv_percent), but for rows from tx_lsl or tx_ec that already have disadvantaged = 'Yes' hardcoded and no disadv_percent column, the ifelse logic evaluates is.na(disadv_percent) as TRUE (column may be missing/NA), so the result depends on whether the already-set disadvantaged column carries through. The logic correctly resolves to 'Yes' only if disadvantaged was pre-set, but this is fragile.
suggestion: Apply the disadvantaged derivation logic separately per source (general vs lead/EC), or use coalesce() to preserve pre-set values before applying the disadv_percent check.

issue: A hardcoded correction changes 'TX00150018' to 'TX0150018' for San Antonio Water System. Neither value is validated against the standard PWSID format (2-letter state code + 7 digits = 9 chars total). 'TX0150018' has 9 chars but 'TX00150018' has 10, suggesting a leading-zero issue. The correct TCEQ format should be verified.
suggestion: Confirm the authoritative PWSID for San Antonio Water System from the SDWIS/state registry and document the source of the correction.

issue: project_name is set to NA for all rows. The dictionary confirms 'No Information' is acceptable, but the final value is NA (R native) rather than the string 'No Information' used for other unavailable fields like project_id and pwsid.
suggestion: For consistency with other 'No Information' fields, consider setting project_name = 'No Information' or document that NA is the intended representation for this field.

issue: requested_amount is set to as.character(NA) which is consistent with the dictionary ('No Information'), but unlike project_id and pwsid it is not passed through replace_na() to become the string 'No Information'.
suggestion: Apply replace_na(requested_amount, 'No Information') for consistency, or confirm that NA is the accepted representation for monetary fields with no data.

issue: funding_amount is set to as.character(NA) but not passed through replace_na(). The dictionary notes 'No Information' for this field. Same inconsistency as requested_amount.
suggestion: Apply replace_na(funding_amount, 'No Information') for consistency.

issue: principal_forgiveness is set to as.character(NA) but not passed through replace_na(). The dictionary notes 'No information' for this field.
suggestion: Apply replace_na(principal_forgiveness, 'No Information') for consistency.

issue: Two hardcoded project_id values ('16061', '16062') have ' | FT: LSLR' appended to their descriptions, and project_id '15554' also gets ' | FT: LSLR' appended. These annotations are not described in the data dictionary and their meaning ('FT') is undocumented in the script.
suggestion: Add a comment explaining what 'FT: LSLR' means and why these specific projects require this annotation, to ensure reproducibility and reviewer clarity.

issue: The dictionary notes that Appendix K of the General IUP was 'missing one project' and the script adds pif_number = '15941' with expecting_funding = 'Yes' as a hardcoded row. While the dictionary confirms this correction, the hardcoded string '15941' has no source citation in the script.
suggestion: Add an inline comment citing the source document or reviewer note that confirmed PIF 15941 was missing from Appendix K.

issue: community_served is set to NA for all rows. The dictionary states this field should name the municipality or county served. suggestion: Confirm that no geographic column in any of the three source appendices can populate community_served, and document this as a known gap for Texas Year 3.

issue: The LSL appendix files (tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl-625-ammendment.csv, tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl-update.csv, tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl.csv) have the column header 'PopulationServed' (no space, with embedded \r in some cases shown as 'Population\rServed'). The script renames 'population_served' to 'population' via rename(), but after clean_names() the column from these files will be 'populationserved' (not 'population_served'), so the rename will silently fail and population will be NA for all LSL rows.
suggestion: Check the actual cleaned column name after clean_names() — it will be 'populationserved' not 'population_served'. Change the rename to: rename(pif_number = pif_no, population = populationserved, pws_id = pws_id_no) or add a preliminary rename before clean_names().

issue: The LSL appendix files (tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl-625-ammendment.csv) use column 'PWS ID No.' which clean_names() converts to 'pws_id_no'. The script renames this to 'pws_id'. However, tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl.csv and tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl-update.csv use column 'PWS ID' (no 'No.'), which clean_names() converts to 'pws_id' — no rename needed there. The script reads only the '625-ammendment' file (tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl-625-ammendment.csv), so the rename to pws_id_no should work for that file, but this discrepancy between file variants is a fragility risk if the source file is ever swapped.
suggestion: Confirm the script is reading exactly tx-y3-appendix-i-lsl-625-ammendment.csv (which has 'PWS ID No.') and not one of the other variants. Add a defensive check or use rename(any_of(...)) to handle both column name variants.

issue: In tx-y3-appendix-k-ec.csv, the Total Project Cost values contain extra internal spaces: '$     3,004,025.00', '$   40,900,000.00', '$   38,940,000.00'. If clean_numeric_string() uses a simple gsub to remove '$' and ',' without also stripping internal spaces before parsing as numeric, these will parse as NA.
suggestion: Ensure clean_numeric_string() strips all whitespace (including internal spaces) before numeric conversion, e.g., gsub('\\s+', '', x) in addition to removing '$' and ','.

issue: In tx-y3-appendix-j-ec.csv, row 5 (Dallas Water Utilities, rank 5) has the Total Project Cost column value as NA (shown as <NA>), but the 'Requested Phase(s)' column appears to contain '$333,000,000.00' — suggesting a column shift/parse error in that row where the cost value landed in the wrong column. The EmergingContaminants column for that row shows '$333,000,000.00' and Total Project Cost is NA.
suggestion: Manually inspect and correct row 5 of tx-y3-appendix-j-ec.csv. The $333,000,000.00 value appears shifted one column left. This row will produce NA project_cost and incorrect emerging_contaminants for Dallas Water Utilities.

issue: tx_ec (from tx-y3-appendix-j-ec.csv) is joined to tx_ec_invite (from tx-y3-appendix-k-ec.csv) by 'rank'. The EC priority list has 15 rows (ranks 1-15) and the invited list has 3 rows (ranks 1-3). The join by rank alone is correct only if ranks are unique within each file and no rank values overlap unexpectedly. However, in tx-y3-appendix-j-ec.csv, rows 4 and 5 both have Points=230 (rank 4=Fort Worth, rank 5=Dallas), so a tie-break could cause rank instability across file versions. More critically, joining only on rank (not on PIF# or entity) means if ranks differ between the two EC files, wrong projects get marked as funded.
suggestion: Verify the EC IUP invited list (Appendix K) contains no PIF numbers; if it does, join on PIF# instead of rank. If rank is the only key, add a data validation step confirming that rank 1-3 entities match between both EC files before proceeding.

issue: In TX_Y3_LSLR_invited_appendix_j.csv, the column is 'PIF No.' which after clean_names() becomes 'pif_no'. The join between tx_lsl and tx_lsl_invite uses c('pif_no', 'rank'). In TX_Y3_LSLR_invited_appendix_j.csv, PIF No. is numeric with range [16050, 16081] and has 24 distinct values out of 25 rows — meaning one PIF number is duplicated. This could cause a many-to-many join issue producing duplicate rows in tx_lsl.
suggestion: Investigate the duplicate PIF No. in TX_Y3_LSLR_invited_appendix_j.csv (24 distinct values, 25 rows). Deduplicate before joining, or add a check for unexpected row count expansion after the join.

issue: Many project description fields across all files contain embedded carriage returns (\r characters visible throughout the data samples). str_squish() collapses whitespace but does not remove \r characters — these will remain embedded in the cleaned project_description strings, potentially causing display issues or downstream parsing errors.
suggestion: Add gsub('\\r', ' ', project_description) or gsub('[\\r\\n]+', ' ', project_description) before str_squish() to normalize line endings in text fields.

issue: Several entity names contain embedded \r characters (e.g., 'Pine Village Public Utility\rDistrict', 'Riverbend Water\rResources District', 'New Horizons\rRanch and\rCenter, Inc.'). str_squish() on the entity column will not remove \r, resulting in borrower values with embedded carriage returns that won't match expected strings in later case_when() checks (e.g., borrower == 'San Antonio Water System').
suggestion: Apply gsub('\\r', ' ', entity) before str_squish() when creating the borrower field, or apply a global \r-stripping step on all character columns after fread().

issue: In tx-y3-iup-appendix-j.csv, the Disadv % column has only one distinct value ('70%') and is 54.7% NA. The disadvantaged logic uses: ifelse(is.na(disadv_percent) & is.na(disadvantaged), 'No', 'Yes'). After clean_names(), 'Disadv %' becomes 'disadv_percent'. The column is read as character (colClasses='character'). The is.na() check should work correctly since non-missing values are the string '70%'. However, if any rows have empty string '' instead of NA, fread with na.strings='' should convert them to NA — this appears handled, but should be verified since the column is 54.7% NA.
suggestion: Confirm that all blank Disadv % cells are being read as NA (not as empty string '') by fread. The na.strings='' parameter should handle this, but spot-check a few rows where disadvantaged='No' to verify.

issue: The project_type classification uses grepl('lsl|lead', project_description, ignore.case=TRUE) to identify Lead projects. Several General IUP project descriptions mention 'lead' in non-LSLR contexts (e.g., 'Lead and Copper sampling', mentions of 'lead trigger level', 'lead service line inventory' in EC project descriptions). This could cause EC projects or General projects to be misclassified as Lead.
suggestion: Review whether any EC IUP projects (already pre-classified as 'Emerging Contaminants' via the mutate before bind_rows) could be overridden. Since project_type case_when checks !is.na(project_type) first, pre-set EC/Lead types are protected. However, for General IUP rows where project_type is NA, the grepl for 'lead' may still misclassify some General projects. Consider tightening the regex (e.g., require 'lead service line' or 'lsl' rather than bare 'lead').

issue: The script corrects San Antonio Water System's PWSID from 'TX00150018' to 'TX0150018'. The data sample shows PWSID values like 'TX0880001' (9 chars) as the standard format. 'TX0150018' is also 9 chars and matches the standard format. The raw value 'TX00150018' (10 chars) appears to be a data entry error with an extra leading zero. This correction looks correct.
suggestion: No change needed for this specific fix, but verify no other PWSID values in the dataset have the same double-zero anomaly by checking for PWS IDs with length != 9 characters.

issue: The General IUP appendix j file (tx-y3-iup-appendix-j.csv) has one row with Total Project Cost of '$497,526,000.00' (Riverbend Water Resources District). This is an outlier nearly 3x the next largest value visible in samples. The clean_numeric_string() function should handle it, but it may warrant a data validation flag for unusually large project costs.
suggestion: Add a data validation check for project_cost values exceeding a reasonable threshold (e.g., > $500M) to flag potential data entry errors or unit mismatches.

issue: The script manually adds PIF 15941 to the invited list with tibble::add_row(pif_number = '15941', expecting_funding = 'Yes'). The pif_number in tx_invite is derived from the 'pif_number' column after clean_names() on tx-y3-iup-appendix-k.csv. In that file, 'PIF #' is numeric (clean_names gives 'pif_number'), and the join is on pif_number. The manually added row uses character '15941'. In tx_ppl, pif_number comes from 'PIF #' (numeric in source) read as character via colClasses='character'. The join should work if both sides are character, but verify that fread with colClasses='character' is converting the numeric PIF # to character string without scientific notation or padding issues.
suggestion: Confirm that PIF # values read via colClasses='character' from both appendix-j and appendix-k files are plain integer strings (e.g., '15941') with no leading/trailing spaces or decimal points (e.g., not '15941.0'). Add as.character(as.integer(...)) normalization if needed.

issue: The LSL IUP files have PIF No. as numeric with range [16050, 16084]. After reading with colClasses='character', these will be character strings. After rename to pif_number, the script applies replace_na(project_id, 'No Information'). There should be no NAs in PIF No. for LSL files (0% NA shown), but the EC IUP (tx-y3-appendix-j-ec.csv) has no PIF number column at all — the script does not assign pif_number for EC rows, so project_id will be NA and correctly replaced with 'No Information' for all EC IUP rows.
suggestion: This behavior appears intentional per the data dictionary ('No information for projects in the SFY25 EC IUP'). Confirm that all 15 EC IUP rows receive project_id = 'No Information' as expected.

issue: The LSL invited appendix (TX_Y3_LSLR_invited_appendix_j.csv) has Points as numeric with decimal values (e.g., 62.99, 60.43, 54.69, 44.78). The General IUP appendix j also has decimal Points (e.g., 123.1, 122.3). The script uses str_squish(points) to create project_score, but since points is read as numeric via fread (before colClasses='character' override), it will be character after colClasses='character'. The numeric representation may include or drop trailing zeros. Verify that str_squish on character-read numeric columns produces consistent score strings.
suggestion: Consider whether project_score should preserve the original string format or be normalized. If scores like '123.1' vs '123.10' matter for display, standardize the formatting explicitly.

issue: tx_ec is assigned list = 'SFY 2025 EC IUP'. The EC IUP join file (tx-y3-appendix-k-ec.csv) only selects rank and expecting_funding — no 'list' column is added for EC invited rows. After bind_rows, EC projects from both the EC IUP appendix and any EC-type projects from the General IUP appendix will have different list values ('SFY 2025 EC IUP' vs 'SFY 2025 General IUP'). This appears intentional but should be verified.
suggestion: Confirm the list column correctly distinguishes EC projects sourced from the EC IUP versus the General IUP, as this affects traceability back to source documents.
